What Happened?

Shares of customer engagement platform Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) jumped 51.2% in the pre-market session after Salesforce agreed to acquire the company (Braze) for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value. Holders of Braze Class A common stock will receive $47.50 per share in cash, a 58.1% premium to the previous session's close of $30.04, the companies announced in a joint press release carried by Business Wire.

In a regulatory Form 8-K filing with the SEC, Braze disclosed that the definitive merger agreement provides for a $300 million termination fee payable by Salesforce and a $191.39 million fee payable by Braze under specified circumstances.Per company statements, the deal is slated to close during Salesforce's fiscal year 2028, subject to Braze stockholder approval and regulatory clearances. The press release added that the combination will integrate Braze's real-time messaging and artificial intelligence features across roughly 2,770 customers into Salesforce's Marketing Cloud and Agentforce platforms.

Is now the time to buy Braze? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Braze's shares are extremely volatile and have had 53 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Braze and indicate this news significantly impacted the market's perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 5.7% on the news that investors shifted their focus from what AI technology can do toward concerns over how companies will finance it.

Driven by these escalating AI funding fears and elevated interest rates, CNBC noted that a massive rotation out of the sector erased more than $1 trillion from the world's largest semiconductor and AI-related stocks this week.

Furthermore, CNBC explained that this funding anxiety triggered counterintuitive moves in the broader market, as investors reassessed the impact of high interest rates on corporate debt-servicing capacity and overall economic growth. Because of these rising structural risks, CNBC reported that safe-haven demand temporarily outweighed inflation fears, prompting capital to exit high-growth tech assets and flow into the Treasury market, which ironically pulled the 10-year Treasury yield down toward 5.09 percent. Ultimately, according to CNBC analysts, this widespread tech sell-off underscores a growing realization on Wall Street that if the capital-intensive AI trade slows due to financing constraints, broader economic growth will likely decelerate as well.

title: Braze Soars 51% on $5.66 Billion Salesforce Deal: “An Opportunity to Wow Your Customers”

Braze Soars 51% on $5.66 Billion Salesforce Deal: “An Opportunity to Wow Your Customers”
Gian Estrada

BRZE
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Braze Soars 51% on $5.66 Billion Salesforce Deal: "An Opportunity to Wow Your Customers" ©Jirsak from Getty Images and coffeekai from Getty Images via Canva

Braze (BRZE:NASDAQ) shares are up about 51% today (trading at about $45.50) after Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) agreed to buy the marketing software company for $47.50 a share in cash.

The number to watch is the price per dollar of sales. Salesforce is paying about 6.2x Braze's revenue guide for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2027. Salesforce itself trades at 4.75x next-twelve-month revenue, a later revenue period, so the two aren't a straight comparison.

The Braze Deal Terms

About $5.66 billion in enterprise value, all cash.

About 58% above Braze's $30.04 Monday close, and about 80% above its 30-day average.

Closing expected in Salesforce's fiscal 2028, which starts February 1, 2027.

No change to Salesforce's fiscal 2027 guidance.

Salesforce would owe Braze a $300 million termination fee in specified cases tied to a permanent regulatory block or a failure to close by the contract deadline, subject to other conditions.

What Salesforce Paid for Braze

Braze traded at 3.14x next-twelve-month revenue before the offer. The deal values it at about 6.2x its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance, but that uses an earlier revenue period than the forward multiples for Adobe (3.43x) and HubSpot (2.70x).

CRM, ADBE, HUBS and BRZE Stock NTM Total Enterprise Value / Revenues (TIKR)

Salesforce is paying up for growth, with Braze revenue up 26.2% last quarter. Profits are thin, though: Braze guides to about $76 million of non-GAAP operating income this year, under 9% of revenue. But the deal is small for the buyer: $5.66 billion is about 2.8% of Salesforce's $199.5 billion market value. An expensive multiple on a cheap check.

Who Else Braze's Price Tag Reprices

Salesforce fell about 3% before the open and was trading near flat, at about $242, by early afternoon. HubSpot climbed about 6%, potentially reflecting renewed takeover interest after the Braze announcement, though Adobe also rose about 2%. Braze's $2 gap to the offer, about 4.4%, says traders expect the deal to close.

HubSpot (HUBS:NYSE) is the name to watch. It went into Tuesday at 2.70x next-twelve-month revenue, below Braze's 3.14x before the offer, and Salesforce still paid a 58% premium for Braze.

Why Klaviyo Stock Rallied Today

Klaviyo (NYSE:KVYO) stock charged sharply higher Tuesday morning, gaining as much as 11.8% in early trading. As of 1:13 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 11.6%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the software-as-a-service (SaaS) specialist higher was the acquisition of a rival in the space.

Image source: Getty Images.

A big deal

In a press release that dropped earlier today, tech bigwig Salesforce announced it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze (NASDAQ:BRZE) for $47.50 per share in an all-cash deal that values the company at $5.66 billion. It also represents a 58% premium over the stock's closing price on Monday.

Braze's customer engagement platform uses predictive intelligence to help marketers build personalized messages and customized ad campaigns to target customers in real time.

So what does this have to do with Klaviyo?

Braze and Klaviyo play in the same sandbox, so to speak, though they have distinct markets. While Braze focuses on mobile apps and digital, Klaviyo specializes in direct-to-consumer marketing for e-commerce providers. Despite their different approaches, the overlap in personalized messaging made them competitors.

Investors see the acquisition of Braze at a significant premium as a validation of Klaviyo's approach, sending shares higher on the news. Furthermore, joining Salesforce will likely shift Braze's focus toward the company's enterprise customers, reducing much of the remaining overlap and increasing the market opportunity for Klaviyo. Moreover, Salesforce's purchase of Braze may stoke interest among other tech buyers, making Klaviyo a potential acquisition target.

Moreover, at 23 times forward earnings, Klaviyo stock is attractively priced.

All three major US stock indexes were up in late-morning trading Tuesday, as oil prices were down, boosting investor sentiment.

In company news, Salesforce (CRM) has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze (BRZE) for an enterprise value of about $5.66 billion. Under the terms of the agreement, shareholders of Braze Class A common stock will receive $47.50 in cash per share. The deal is expected to close in fiscal year 2028. Salesforce shares were down 1.3% around midday, while Braze shares were up 50.9%.

General Motors (GM) reported Q3 adjusted earnings Tuesday of $3.70 per diluted share, up from $2.80 a year earlier and above the FactSet consensus analyst estimate of $3.69. Third-quarter revenue was $50.02 billion, up from $48.59 billion a year ago and above the FactSet consensus of $48.78 billion. For 2026, the company narrowed its adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $12.75 to $13.75 from $12 to $14. Analysts expect $13.47. Meanwhile, General Motors completed its $6 billion share repurchase program announced in January, and its board has approved a new $20 million multi-year buyback plan. GM shares were down 6.5%.

GE Aerospace (GE) reported Q3 EPS Tuesday of $2.25, up from $1.66 a year earlier and above the FactSet consensus of $2.01. Third-quarter revenue was $14.12 billion, up from $12.18 billion a year ago and above the FactSet consensus of $12.88 billion. The company raised its adjusted EPS guidance to between $8 and $8.10 from its previous forecast of $7.65 to $7.85. Analysts expect $7.94. GE shares were down 4.3%.

Amazon.com (AMZN) said Tuesday it's hiring over 300,000 people for seasonal, part-time and full-time work across the US during the holiday season. Starting on Jan. 1, 2027, seasonal workers will earn $20 per hour on average, the company said. Staff who work at least 30 hours per week will have access to healthcare coverage, it said. For full-time employees wages will start at $20 per hour and reach an average of nearly $24 per hour, the company said. Amazon shares were up 0.4%.

3M (MMM) reported Q3 adjusted EPS Tuesday of $2.50, up from $2.23 a year earlier and above the FactSet consensus of $2.38. Net Q3 sales were $6.58 billion, up from $6.52 billion a year ago but below the FactSet consensus of $6.61 billion. For 202, the company expects adjusted EPS of $9.10 to $9.15, up from its previous guidance of $8.80 to $8.95 and above the FactSet consensus of $8.94. 3M shares were up 5.2%.
